messages:
acme-batch-runner: Hey team — running into massive 429s on our nightly embedding job. Started last night after scaling workers from 4 -> 32. Job: ~2M strings, model: text-embedding-3-small. getting intermittent 429s and some responses that claim dimension mismatch. logs attached below.

sarah-support: sorry you're blocked — can you paste the exact error payload you get? Also which endpoint (hosted/dedicated/private)?

acme-batch-runner: Hosted API in us-west. Error logs: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 10
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1912345660
{"error":"rate limit exceeded","detail":"burst capacity exhausted"}
```
Also occasionally see: 
```
400 Bad Request {"error":"dimension_mismatch","detail":"expected 1536 but got 3072"}
```
We didn't change model config — same job has run before. The 3072 is surprising.

olivia-sre: thanks — two immediate suspects: 1) client library or batching code accidentally concatenating vectors or sending embeddings as vector payloads (server expects raw texts not vectors) causing dimension errors, 2) concurrency + batching hitting a per-account burst token bucket.

luis-eng-runtime: quick note on the hosted quotas: there is a per-minute token/embedding-unit burst bucket + sustained rate. Burst will allow short spikes but multiple concurrent workers with large batch sizes can deplete it fast. The X-RateLimit headers look like you exhausted the remaining tokens for that window. Reset at 1912345660.

tyler-cs: acme, can you share the client code that spawns workers and the batch size? A lot of customers hit this when they parallelize workers *and* use large embedding batch_size.

acme-batch-runner: simplified snippet: 
```python
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
def send_batch(batch):
    client.embeddings.create(model='text-embedding-3-small', input=batch)

with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=32) as ex:
    for b in chunks(stream_generator(), 256):
        ex.submit(send_batch, b)
```
We used `chunks(..., 256)` and 32 workers.

sarah-support: ok that's a lot of parallel requests and very large batches. Two separate issues likely:
- bursting many large requests concurrently will multiply alleged token consumption and blow through the burst bucket.
- dimension error might be from a different code path — are you ever calling embeddings endpoint with already-embedded vectors or using a different model name in another job?

luis-eng-runtime: to reproduce locally we suggest: run 20 parallel workers with batch_size 256 against hosted with a short window. We have an internal repro script sample: 
```
# repro.sh
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  python stress_embed.py --batch 256 &
done
wait
```
stress_embed.py uses same client call above. That reliably yields 429s in 60-90s in our sandbox.

acme-batch-runner: how should we change backoff/retry? right now client retries immediately 

sarah-support: use exponential backoff + jitter and respect Retry-After header. Example: start 500ms, multiply x2, jitter +/- 20%, cap at 30s. Also limit concurrency and shrink batch size. Most customers hit best cost/latency with batch sizes 16-64 at concurrency ~4-8.

olivia-sre: adding to that: recommend adding a client-side leaky bucket to smooth bursts. Key fields from headers to watch: `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, and `Retry-After` — if Remaining==0, pause until Reset. We can also implement a central coordinator process to ensure only N inflight embed requests.

acme-batch-runner: thanks — we rolled back to 8 workers and batch_size=64 and retried; still see occasional 429s but much fewer. We also got a single dimension mismatch again after a long run: 
```
400 {"error":"dimension_mismatch","detail":"expected 1536 but got 3072"}
```
Any clue?

luis-eng-runtime: that one makes me suspect two different model variants being hit in the same account. Are you pinning model by name or using a floating alias? If you switched to a larger model in another job, cached responses or a routed fallback might produce vectors of a different size. Can you grep recent requests for model names?

acme-batch-runner: grep shows one cron job uses `text-embedding-3-large` (3072) for a different dataset. But those jobs run on a different schedule, not same time. Could our worker reuse a batch payload or mis-label?

olivia-sre: also check if your pipeline sometimes passes precomputed vectors into the embeddings endpoint (accidentally re-embedding). A symptom is sending a JSON where the items are arrays instead of strings. Add server-side validation on client before call, e.g.: 
```
for item in batch:
  if isinstance(item, list):
    raise ValueError('unexpected vector payload')
```

acme-batch-runner: good call — we found a stray map step that cached intermediate vectors for dedup and accidentally yielded them into the batch generator when cache hit. Fixing that eliminated the dimension errors.

sarah-support: great. For the remaining 429s, two routes: 1) client smoothing (reduce workers/batch size + backoff + leaky bucket) — immediate remediation; 2) request quota/burst increase or Dedicated plan for sustained throughput. I can open an account change request if you want.

acme-batch-runner: we tried client smoothing, but our nightly window is tight — would like to request temporary burst increase for tonight (2x) to finish backlog.

sarah-support: filing request now — pinging @luis-eng-runtime to confirm if temporary burst lift is possible from infra side.

luis-eng-runtime: I can approve a limited temporary increase for your account for tonight (2x burst) — will need start/end times and expected throughput. Please send ETA and list of worker IPs if you want IP-based rules.

acme-batch-runner: start 1912346400, end 1912350000, expected avg concurrency 12, batch_size 64. IPs: 52.45.12.8, 52.45.12.9.

ratebot: [automated] quota-change-request created: #Q-4821, assigned to luis-eng-runtime, status: pending-approve.

olivia-sre: final notes for playbook: 
- enforce schema in client to avoid vector re-submission
- cap concurrency to 8 unless on Dedicated
- batch size 16-64 recommended (depends on latency budget)
- backoff: exp backoff + jitter + respect Retry-After
- when requesting quota lifts, provide time window and IPs.

sarah-support: closing loop — acme please confirm after tonight if the temporary lift worked and whether you want to migrate heavy nightly loads to Dedicated or add scheduling to avoid sustained bursts. :thumbsup:

acme-batch-runner: will confirm tomorrow — thanks all for the fast turnaround! :heart:
